title: From Rio's Streets to the Grand Prize: How Nay Dassi Brought Carnival to Life in CLO
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/fac0d5f2cf8f43b6be7bd006089fb249/images/846a753d29e3436188ef0965cd49d5a1Banner%20Nay%201.png)_This year, our community celebrated creativity and cultural expression through the Carnival Design Contest. Designers were invited to capture the vibrant spirit of Carnival and bring their ideas to life using CLO. The contest received inspiring submissions that showcased not only technical skill but also the imagination and unique perspectives of creators from our community._

## _We spoke with the grand winner, Nay Dassi (_[_WarpAtelie_](https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/490999/collection/collections) _), to learn more about his journey, the inspiration behind his winning design, and the creative process that turned his vision into a Carnival look full of personality._

* * *

![b145017d6629415b97d6ce7e76ccd7a1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/fac0d5f2cf8f43b6be7bd006089fb249/images/b145017d6629415b97d6ce7e76ccd7a1Nay.png)

  
**Can you introduce yourself and share a bit about your journey as a designer?  
** My name is Nayson Dassi, and I’ve been a fashion designer for almost 12 years. Today, I work with prints and digital fashion, serving brands across different niches. This May will mark one year since I started creating directly for the end consumer at Warp. All pieces are designed in 3D and sewn by me, turning Warp into a phygital atelier. With digital fashion, I can deliver truly original pieces with well-crafted finishes and techniques.

**What inspired your Carnival design? What story or energy did you want to capture?**  
I’ve always experienced Carnival from a distance. I’m not into street parties or samba, but I’ve always found it magical and beautiful. I’m from Rio Grande do Sul, but I lived in Rio de Janeiro and experienced the city beyond its tourist side. That’s when I saw a _Bate-Bola_ for the first time, and it amazed me. It stood out in the middle of a street parade passing my house, and I instantly fell in love.

![563e52360bea4ee4920e36b6d3207631](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/fac0d5f2cf8f43b6be7bd006089fb249/images/563e52360bea4ee4920e36b6d3207631IMG_8026.jpg)![4c58ce4da80648d3b45fe4449a86b56d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/fac0d5f2cf8f43b6be7bd006089fb249/images/4c58ce4da80648d3b45fe4449a86b56dMoodboard%20%281%29.png)

* * *

**What was the first element you developed, and how did the design evolve?  
** From the start, I knew I wanted to create a _Bate-Bola_ costume. I sketched out rough ideas and immediately started modeling everything in CLO. I like to work by putting ideas into practice quickly. I visualize the concept in my head, then start thinking about patterns and structure. I work organically, experimenting and adjusting along the way until the piece feels right.

**Did you face any creative challenges during the process? How did you overcome them?  
** At first, I considered a costume with lots of fringes, but the process and result didn’t work. That led me to focus more on prints and textures. When I hit a block in development, I move to another stage and return later to see if the problem really needs attention or if it works in context. I’m flexible—I don’t believe in perfect work; sometimes you have to let go of certain details.

![e3c7f6ddb876444f858a805620627364](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/fac0d5f2cf8f43b6be7bd006089fb249/images/e3c7f6ddb876444f858a805620627364Captura%20de%20tela%202026-03-20%20012444.png)

![22c5dae7453d43df950b6c9952eda73f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/fac0d5f2cf8f43b6be7bd006089fb249/images/22c5dae7453d43df950b6c9952eda73fCaptura%20de%20tela%202026-03-20%20012522.png)

**Was there a moment when CLO allowed you to do something that would have been impossible physically?  
** The entire project. A _Bate-Bola_ costume is structurally complex and can take months to create, often passed down generation to generation. Today, I can’t imagine creating without testing first in 3D. I only go physical if I’ve done something similar before. For new designs, CLO gives me confidence—I can test, experiment, and see how it works before making it physically.

**Carnival pieces are known for their detail, color, and volume. What was the biggest challenge translating this into CLO?  
** I’ve built a solid foundation in CLO and always try to keep files light for smooth simulation. I rely on visual shortcuts to convey realism while keeping the file manageable. For this project, I used the “strengthen” function to give structure to almost the entire costume,

**Which CLO tools or features were most important for bringing your vision to life?  
** The “strengthen” function was key for structure, along with interfacings and carefully marked topstitching for realism. These also allowed me to experiment with prints directly in CLO, sometimes even adjusting colors on the fly.

![bc4c5771da69433fae4685211c12bdbd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/fac0d5f2cf8f43b6be7bd006089fb249/images/bc4c5771da69433fae4685211c12bdbdCaptura%20de%20tela%202026-03-20%20012614.png)

**Which part of the design are you most proud of technically, and why?  
** Every detail excites me—the stripes, fixed fringes, and the weave that reveals the avatar underneath. One hand holds a ball, the other a themed umbrella. I designed every print, from elaborate motifs to polka dots and stripes. I loved being able to include all the ideas in my head, even transforming my atelier’s logo into a giant headpiece layered with another headpiece underneath. It was pure fun and creativity.

* * *

![2082f6a547fa46beaae4774e63807bc2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/fac0d5f2cf8f43b6be7bd006089fb249/images/2082f6a547fa46beaae4774e63807bc2MACAC%C3%83O%20BASE%20-%20Copia%20-%20Copia_1.png)

**What advice would you give designers hesitant to start with 3D or enter contests like this?  
** You only learn by doing. CLO gave me the autonomy and confidence to model in ways I never had before. Today, I only take on projects for brands that embrace CLO or 3D. The market is moving fast—those who adapt thrive; those who don’t, fall behind. Just start, however you can. I began designing prints on my phone and gradually built my atelier with every opportunity the market gave me. It’s not easy, but it’s far more rewarding than just wishing.

**What’s next? Are there projects you’re excited about?  
** I’m launching Warp’s winter collection with pieces modeled and rendered in CLO, using AI 3D avatars. The designs are wide, bold, and feature exclusive prints I created. This time, they have more visibility than last year, and I hope to produce even more. I’m thrilled to release these new pieces and sew the upcoming orders.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: It is great to see a bit of the process! Great project! Congratulations 👏👏👏
content_description: Showcasing the inspiring journey and creative process of Nay Dassi, grand winner of the Carnival Design Contest, as he brings vibrant Carnival spirit to life through innovative 3D fashion design in CLO.

title: AI fashion film with endless expressions using CLO3D
content:
![c74c312324a447318878b89ff77a3db3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/0fad0cec88f04cc9a63905982bed6164/images/c74c312324a447318878b89ff77a3db3%EB%91%90_%EB%AA%A8%EB%8D%B8%EC%9D%B4_%EB%93%B1%EC%9D%84_202604060511%20%281%29.png)Hello, this time at the university, I will give a special lecture on making fashion film videos using CLO3D and AI.  
  
So I'm making a sample video, and I want to feel this feeling with others how comfortable it is to make a fashion film video with CLO3D.  
  
Since AI is developing very rapidly and many people are using it, there may be many people who already know what we are going to talk about now. But if you're new to it, I think this can be helpful.  
![3a0d8720e1d2401da64e75f425a9fe48](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/0fad0cec88f04cc9a63905982bed6164/images/3a0d8720e1d2401da64e75f425a9fe48%EB%91%90_%EB%AA%A8%EB%8D%B8%EC%9D%B4_%EB%93%B1%EC%9D%84_202604060511.png)

  
Until now, I mainly used AI after rendering the front photo.  
However, AI finds that it understands much better when images rendered from multiple angles are mixed in one image.

![3f0ccda8489643038904e068d626dd01](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/0fad0cec88f04cc9a63905982bed6164/images/3f0ccda8489643038904e068d626dd01Model2.jpg)The above picture is an image that is rendered at each angle in CLO3D and then replaced with each model, and is woven into a single image file in Photoshop.  
  
When I inserted an image made of one image into Asset, it was so convenient to make a complete video that did not deteriorate.  
  
There's one more thing I need to tell you: your pose doesn't have to be upright.  
![238fac5b606341d292bf6ba76846e854](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/0fad0cec88f04cc9a63905982bed6164/images/238fac5b606341d292bf6ba76846e854Harf%20Suit.png)The first image I rendered was standing with my legs placed close by like this.  
  
But AI recognized this as a skirt, and I changed it to a leg-open pose to make it clear that it was a pair of pants, so I made a new rendered.  
  
This image is an asset for utilizing the design of the costume and the face of the model, so it doesn't matter if you use a deformed pose.  
  
However, if it's an avatar pose where the design of the costume can be clearly seen.  
  
If you're a video creator with AI, make sure to check this out. It's a simple and wonderful way for AI to prevent errors in damaging and transforming your work.  
  


YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ks8RtYZD4i0

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hello! It looks very realistic. Could you please tell me what program you used to make the video?
Reply 1: Of course! The video's scene production was made using Flow AI Platform's Veo. For editing, Premiere pro was used.

Comment 2: These AI tips are going to be so helpful! I usually get frustrated and give up because the results never turn out the way I want, but I’ll definitely try your method!
Reply 1: Awesome! I'm listing the caveats as I prepare for the special lecture, and the content is more than I thought. I'll keep organizing the things that would be nice to share.
content_description: This page introduces a special university lecture on creating fashion film videos using CLO3D and AI, demonstrating practical tips for optimizing 3D renders and AI integration to enhance video production quality.

title: Help with Compression Sleeve
content:
Hey everyone, I’m an industrial design student doing my first soft goods project and have been watching a bunch of tutorials on CLO. I am running into trouble with Clo3d . It’s my first time using a fabric CAD program. I’m designing a performance legging sleeve and can’t get the fabric to stop falling and to stick to the avatar. I have measured the fabric to ensure it is fit the user but am experiencing falling and once i got it to fit am experiencing wrinkling. Below I have attached reference images of the error and also the file in case anyone wants to take a look at it ![d4b932877d67427785bee8e1b2101224](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a1db1e575eb94e0fb3f79b2cc9d22f69/images/d4b932877d67427785bee8e1b2101224Sleeve%201.png)![34f150d571b648209fcf335e3fd2151c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a1db1e575eb94e0fb3f79b2cc9d22f69/images/34f150d571b648209fcf335e3fd2151cSleeve%202.png)![d9d63a996f33422d9f37ef268c13af35](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a1db1e575eb94e0fb3f79b2cc9d22f69/images/d9d63a996f33422d9f37ef268c13af35Sleeve%20patterm.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you Melody. Slimming the pattern fixed that problem. I'm sorry for all of the questions but this has been helpful. I do have a few more if you dont mind. I am trying to create this embedded channels in the garment and have created another pocket, i messed around with the superimpose under and over + decreasing pressure on the pocket, it has worked a little. Just dealing with the stretch of the fabric pulling the pocket, maybe the strengthen feature will help with that?I am also building these bands that will run under the sleeve in a channel, but i am running into issues with it, i built it from internal lines and fabric cuts but i am thinking maybe needs to be made from a regular rectangle I included reference images of a band type of layout but mine wouldnt be sewn to the pants I would have these channels.Let me know if there is a better channel of communication i could really use some advice as the timeline is nearing end.

Comment 2: Hi, you can temporary create a measurment line on the avatar at the position you want you piece to be and attach the pattern top line to that measurement line. But this I a temporary solution to get a first look. you pattern piece need to be about 20 to 30% smaller then to bodymeasumernent to have a compression effect and you need to apply a stretch fabric. And all the other things Melody mentioned. After doing this you can detach the pattern from the avatar and it should stay in place
content_description: A space for an industrial design student to share challenges and seek advice on fabric simulation issues in CLO3D while developing a performance legging sleeve.

**Showcase Your Talent, Unlock Opportunities**

The **Next Gen Hub** is a curated space designed to highlight the next generation of creative leaders. We provide students and early-career creators with a professional platform to spotlight their work, gain industry recognition, and connect directly with companies seeking fresh talent.

![13b7a07daf6d4678a350a09905bf3b7f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/f760ee3144a24710aaa6176173f82111/images/13b7a07daf6d4678a350a09905bf3b7fimage%20%287%29.png)

We are looking for passionate creators who are ready to make their mark. You are eligible if you fall into any of the following categories:

  * **Students or Recent Graduates**




Currently enrolled in or newly graduated from a design or creative field.  


  * **Self-Taught Visionaries**




Independent creators building their first professional portfolio.

Professionals transitioning into a brand-new creative discipline.

title: Python API ImportAvatarMeasurement() always returns False on Mac + headless video export
content:
Hi everyone,

I'm a PhD student at UC Davis using CLO 2025.2.330 Standalone Academic on Mac. I'm building an ML dataset of garment simulation videos across different body shapes using the Python API. I've contacted CLO support (ticket 135471) and they directed me here. I have two blockers I can't resolve:

Issue 1: ImportAvatarMeasurement() always returns False

I have tried every combination of .avs and .avt files including:

  * US_ASTM Missy/Petite/Plus .avs files with FV2.1_Yuna.avt

  * Custom-saved .avs files with FV2.1_Yuna.avt

  * Exported mannequin .avt with various .avs files




Code used:

import import_api, ApiTypes

opt = ApiTypes.ImportExportOption()

result = import_api.ImportAvatarMeasurement(avs_path, avt_path, opt)

print(result) # always False

Issue 2: ExportAnimationVideo() cannot save headlessly on Mac

ExportAnimationVideo(path) always opens a Qt dialog that cannot be automated. Calling with no arguments returns a path but the file is never written (no Xvid codec on Mac). How do we export animation videos headlessly from Python on Mac?

Any working code examples would be greatly appreciated.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hello, ajrichardsonThe ImportAvatarMeasurement API is currently implemented to be available for enterprise customers.Upon checking, ExportAnimationVideo is implemented to simply open the dialog for that feature. We will internally discuss providing a new API for this functionality.
content_description: This page serves to seek expert guidance and code examples for resolving issues with CLO 3D's Python API related to importing avatar measurements and headless animation video export on Mac.

title: Render stopped!!
content:
Hello!

I let my macbook pro rendering all night but it stopped. I’m doing a turntable animation. And it’s weird cause the rendering clock is still going but the progress is frozen.

Do i have to restart the rendering? 😭😭![74581d6e7fef43858a07ff7d2465731d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/1a77632b39ec4061bbb3708337e61cc6/images/74581d6e7fef43858a07ff7d2465731dIMG_2371.jpeg)![3a9cf701935d41d8b97aa203bce56838](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/1a77632b39ec4061bbb3708337e61cc6/images/3a9cf701935d41d8b97aa203bce56838IMG_2372.jpeg)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you all for the response!! I had no idea i could re render the remaining frames i'll definitely try that

Comment 2: Yes, that's right. You can check if there are sequence frame pictures in the folder you specified. If so, you only need to re - render the remaining dozen or so pictures. It seems that it's relatively stable on Mac. You can render so many frames at once, while on Windows, it gets stuck when rendering over a hundred frames.

Comment 3: From the picture, it seems that the render for 346 sheets is completed. If you check CLO Asset Folder, the image will exist. I think you only need to proceed with the additional 14 sheets of render after it stopped working.You must have been worried a lot because a lot of time has passed, but I hope you don't worry too much.Cheer up!👏
content_description: A community support page for troubleshooting MacBook Pro rendering issues during turntable animations.

title: Burton contest
content:
I have a doubt. we are two friends and can we join and work together for the Burton competition as a team and submit entries as a team?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, that shouldn't be a problem at all!You'll just need to pick one person to be the official 'uploader' on CONNECT. As long as you credit both of yourselves in the entry details, submitting as a duo is totally fine. Good luck to you both!

title: Clo trial for Burton contest
content:
Is there a wayfor me to get a trial copy of Clo without having to input my card details for the **_Burton Contest?_**

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, it’s not possible to sign up for the CLO free trial without providing your card details. However, what you can do is cancel the subscription immediately after signing up.By doing this, you will still have full access to the software for the duration of the trial period for the Burton Contest, but it will ensure the plan doesn't automatically renew or charge your card once the trial ends.
Reply 1: Hi Lucile, thanks for the suggestion. I will go with that.
content_description: This page provides information on obtaining a trial copy of Clo for the Burton Contest without requiring credit card details.
